newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Too soon to determine gold deposit size - CVRD.
newsitem.headline: Too soon to determine gold deposit size - CVRD.

text.p: Brazil's state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) said it was too early to evaluate the mineral content of a new deposit in Para state, which a newspaper said contained 300 tonnes of gold.

In a statement prepared for the stock exchanges and made available to Reuters, CVRD confirmed the existence of minerals deep beneath the soil at Igarape-Bahia, but said its surveys had not advanced far enough to evaluate the find.
"We confirm the existence of minerals, at depth, at that place," the company said. "However, it should be noted, the indications are promising but still not conclusive."
Globo newspaper reported Friday that the deposit could contain 300 tonnes of gold and 300 tonnes of copper.
The new reserve, if confirmed, lies near CVRD's largest operational gold mine and 150 km from Serra Pelada, site of the world's largest gold rush in the 1980s.

If found to contain 300 tonnes of gold, it would be twice aslarge as the estimated reserves of Serra Leste, the most recent gold discovery announced amid fanfare by the government last February and situated next door to Serra Pelada.
CVRD said it had carried out six exploratory borings and found minerals in two. Six further borings are being undertaken.
CVRD said it still had to carry out extensive surveys and calculations, as well as technical evaluations of the viability of production.
"None of these stages has yet been undertaken. Therefore, it is premature to affirm that we have already proven the existence of mineral resources at Igarape-Bahia," the CVRD statement said.
